title: Start Dates, Amendment Leads and Claimant Notice under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders
content:
A deduction under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders does not apply to a benefit payment the moment the election or order is recorded. Each kind has a lead time, counted in business days from the day the election or order is recorded, before it applies to payments issued; a separate lead time applies when an order is amended or an election is changed; and for the agency kinds the claimant is mailed notice a set number of calendar days before the first deduction.

| Kind | Lead before a new election or order applies to payments issued | Lead before an amended order or changed election applies | Notice mailed to the claimant before the first deduction | Deduction from payments issued before the effective date | When a change in the state withholding rate takes effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Voluntary Federal Income Tax Withholding | 2 business days | 2 business days | 0 — no notice period | Not allowed | Not applicable |
| Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding | 2 business days | 2 business days | 0 — no notice period | Not allowed | From the first payment of the calendar year |
| Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order | 5 business days | 5 business days | At least 10 calendar days | Not allowed | Not applicable |
| Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order | 5 business days | 5 business days | At least 10 calendar days | Not allowed | Not applicable |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error | 10 business days | 10 business days | At least 10 calendar days | Not allowed | Not applicable |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation | 10 business days | 10 business days | At least 10 calendar days | Not allowed | Not applicable |

### What the columns mean for the claimant

- **New elections and orders.** The lead in the second column is the number of business days after the election or order is recorded before it applies to payments issued. Voluntary income tax elections run on 2 business days, child support orders on 5, and SNAP Overissuance Recovery orders on 10.
- **Amendments and changes.** When an order is amended or an election is changed, the new amount applies only after the lead in the third column, counted from the day the amendment or change is recorded. For every kind that lead equals the kind's lead for a new election or order.
- **Notice.** A claimant subject to a child support or SNAP Overissuance Recovery order is mailed notice at least 10 calendar days before the first deduction. The two voluntary kinds have no notice period (0).
- **No retroactive deduction.** No kind allows a deduction to be taken for payments issued before the effective date.
- **State withholding rate.** For Voluntary State Income Tax Withholding, a change in the state withholding rate takes effect from the first payment of the calendar year. The column does not apply to the other five kinds.

### Comparison across kinds (derived from the table)

| Kind group | Business-day lead, new | Business-day lead, amended | Calendar-day notice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Voluntary income tax (federal and state) | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| Child support (current and arrears-only) | 5 | 5 | 10 |
| SNAP Overissuance Recovery (both kinds) | 10 | 10 | 10 |

Note the difference in units: the leads are counted in business days, while the notice period is counted in calendar days.
